lessons: Range calls failed on trend days (3, 5, 6, 17 Nov up; 23 Nov down): option walls are where price may stall, not a fence. Never lean against the trend printed by desk_brief.py; when a wall breaks, follow the break.
Flip-flopping lost money (17 Nov: 11 calls in a day; 25-26 Nov lean flipped up/down/up). One call per session, changed only when its stop is hit; at most one replacement, then stay out.
Stops 60-100 points away were hit by normal noise while direction was right. Stops and range edges are sized from dayMove (min_stop, min_half_range in desk_brief.py), never tighter.
'Right on the box only' flattered the record. A call with a lean is right only if the lean paid.

days.nifty: Four scored: 54 wrong, 55 wrong, 56 right, 57 right. 54 leaned up off Thursday's close while the 5-day trend was flat and Friday opened 45 lower, so the lean never paid. 55 put its range edges 106 and 144 points from spot, half the 202-point minimum, and the floor broke within the hour.
days.bank: Two scored: 31 right, 32 wrong. 32 called a no-lean range with the trend down on the day and the week, and its floor sat 396 points from spot, under the 497-point minimum; the 63,000 floor gave way by 42 points.
days.change: Monday's Nifty call is a no-lean range with edges 257 and 293 points from spot; Bank Nifty leans down with the trend and gives no buy zone.
